faces.f: The people of Amrou were scattered by war and driven into hiding. Scouts maintain the beacon fires that signal "return" and "home."
The paradise of Amrou Haven had become a field of cinders. Its people struggled to survive, hoping to see visions of its past in the strange storms that quickly passed.
"My people swore to protect Benalia to the end. It is battered, but yet stands, as do we."
"My pride may be gone, but our hunt is not over."
A fight put off forever is already won.
"Each place we see is as ruined and lifeless as the last. So here we stay, because this ruin is *ours*."

"We have a proud history of self-sacrifice. But it is easy, in these bleak times, to find one among us who is eager to die for any cause."
—Tavalus, acolyte of Korlis
Crovax was destined for an angel's curse, but one warped timeline saw the noble redeemed.
"Heed my words, traveler. Plagues, war, desolation . . . all mere hints of what is yet to come from Dominaria's vault of horrors."

"Where metal is tainted and wood is scarce, we are best armed by faith."
—Tavalus, acolyte of Korlis
Its skin remains in a flowing, liquid state that keeps its body coated with potent restorative lymph.

"Those who seek to upset the balance must be taxed for such ambitions."
—Verithain, mesa high priest
"I have been brought to this place and I cannot leave. I may be free of the amber, but I am still in prison."

"Its broad claw suggests a chitinous shield, but in fact it conceals glands that secrete a remarkably swift healing agent."
—Rukarumel, field journal
Like a great bellows it hisses, and its kin, both living and dead, are lifted to safety.

"I cannot teach you their brand of magic, but I can teach you how to defend against it."
—Tavalus, priest of Korlis
Some timelines forever fray, branch, and intermingle. Others end abruptly.
Dominaria erodes with each passing gust.
He remembers a past of light and healing. But he lives the bitter present—parching salt, scouring wind, and the withering heat of the desert.

"Those who endure in the face of suffering, those whose faith shines long in evil days, they shall see salvation."
—*Song of All*, canto 904

"They encircled our patrol with the stealth of snakes, corralling us like livestock."
—Merrik Aidar, Benalish patrol
As the muscle cords of the creature twitched, Hanna saw an unsettling unanimity in the others' rippling flesh. She didn't know what it meant, but she urged Sisay to keep the ship at a safe distance.

"It's easy for the innocent to speak of justice. They seldom feel its terrible power."
—Orim, Samite inquisitor

"I have spied them, wandering and watching—but for what? I fear they watch for us."
—Yonat of Amrou
Saltfield nomads call a sudden storm a "whitemane."

"Teferi snapped his fingers, and the viashino started clucking like a chicken. Silly, yes, but exactly the thing we needed to break the stifling tension."
—Jhoira, master artificer
A well-made homunculus grooms the mind of its master, pruning the thoughts that lead to madness. Few loredelvers survive the study of the infinite without one.
Water calls to water, and the world is left exhausted and withered in its wake.

"Sages who take the time to verify their sources are rewarded for their diligence."
—Jhoira, to Teferi
They wait in darkened depths, laughing eagerly.
What happens when it is the dream that wakes and the sleeper that fades into memory?
He's mastered the art of sleight of land.
They study the deeds of their traitorous ancestors, hoping the stories may reveal a way back to the physical world.
Wind time's watch, and watch time unwind.

"Belief matters more than truth. Every moment, belief in imaginary things alters lives while truth sits unnoticed and waits."
—Hakim, Loreweaver
"Such sloppy work. Let's unravel it and try again!"
Unable to touch items of value, he goes forth to steal secrets instead.
Those gifted with the sight have one eye in the present and the other in the future.
Those who expect betrayal at every turn are seldom disappointed.
Some spellcrafting mistakes go on to become spells of their own.
Tocasia brushed the gears and cogs from the table. There, before two wide-eyed brothers, she began a lesson on raw elemental magic.

"A horrible sight, yes, but the sounds . . . Its twanging tendons and grinding gears are almost musical."
—Brudiclad, Telchor engineer

"If it returns years hence, our knowledge of how to combat it will be that much greater."
—Andorel, Tolarian sentinel
Drakelings fish with their tails, angling to snare succulent thoughts and memories on their psychic hooks.
As fickle as lightning, as slippery as an eel.
To save this plane, he must forsake all others.

"Great books are meant to be read, then read again backwards or upside down!"
—Ettovard, Tolarian archivist
"It is not just our people I try to rescue. It is our culture, and our hope that we can return to greatness."
His marvels of artifice pale in comparison to the developing machinery of his mind.

"I swear the clouds were created just so the drakes would have a place to lurk."
—Kasharri, skyknight
An eyeblink later, all that remained of the tree-beast was the breeze of its momentum.
The rulers of old Dominaria kept assassins on retainer. However, the true loyalty of these master killers was always to their peers. This elite community survived the fall of the old royal order.
One croaked sermon spreads propaganda and plague.
Her blades slashed across the noble's shadow. He scoffed, then fell over dead.
Those who forget the horrors of the past are doomed to re-meet them.
Tales of the outlaw's cruelty and might grew more embellished with each crime.
Just a small touch of magic can harness the debilitating power of Urborg's poisonous winds.
Every new evincar cements their power with a culling as the weak are purged anew from Rath.

"An army has filled the valley, but it's not like any army I've ever seen. There are no tents, no fires, no horses . . . just a sea of bodies, writhing and moaning, as if a pestilent village were sent to invade us."
—Onean scout

"They are quick to offer advice, those whose mistakes doomed them to undeath. How can I not listen to the wisdom of failure?"
—Ratadrabik of Urborg
A hero fails, a martyr falls. Time twists and destinies interchange.
"The undead are not 'awakened.' They are evicted when there is no room left in the pit for more bodies."

"This soil knows well the taste of the dead. Give it the hunger for a living meal, and it can become a deadly ally."
—Ezrith, druid of the Dark Hours
Tangling vines, fetid murk, paralyzing poisons, and crawling dead. The swamp is nature's trap waiting to be exploited by unnatural minds.

"It offers but a taste of the power that the shadows have to offer. But even that is a heady wine indeed."
—Ratadrabik of Urborg
The living is all it eats.
Most living things were weakened and stunted in the ruinous aftermath of the Phyrexian invasion, but a few grew more horrid than ever.
Death is only the beginning of the end.

"Great losses often bring only a numb shock. To truly plunge a victim into misery, you must overwhelm them with many small sufferings."
—Ratadrabik of Urborg

"What good is your blade without your breath?"
—Greht, Gathan warlord
The lamps on Wyndmoor Street snuff themselves at midnight and refuse to relight, afraid to illuminate what lies in the darkness.
In the stronghold's dungeons, the shadows hide in the vermin.
Some mages tapped into the time rifts, forcing upon others alternate timelines in which unimaginable horrors befall them.

"Even swamps need sustenance. We will give it to them, and in turn, they will sustain us."
—Ezrith, druid of the Dark Hours
When it ran out of bodies, it broke down the crypt door and sought new sustenance.
At the epicenter of the Rathi overlay, the City of Traitors did not align with Dominaria. Many of its inhabitants were caught between the two worlds.
"I have become a gourmet of sorts. Each soul has its own distinctive flavor. The art is in inviting the right company to the feast."
"I have an eternity to know the souls who are bound here, to behold their every facet. But moments from now they will be gagged and masked, and they shall be known by none other."
The time rifts remind Yavimaya of the enemies of its past and provide fresh fuel for its fires.
Covered with hard shell-like plates, these slivers burrow through solid rock to carve out new nests for their hives.

As the time streams grew more and more unstable, Dominaria's creatures struggled to adapt. The intense pressures led to many dead ends but also to lethal new forms that appeared as suddenly as the ashen rains.
Blood, bone, and sinew are magnified, as is the rage that drives them. The brain, however, remains unchanged—a little bean, swinging by a strand in a cavernous, raving head.
Elementals flourished as Dominaria healed and new forms of life adapted to the land's reinfusion with mana.

"The day is mine! I sent three such creatures against my foe, then watched as my magefire popped her soldiers like overripe spleenfruits."
—Dobruk the Unstable, pyromancer
It's never just *one* goblin.

"A rift opened, and our arrows were abruptly stilled. To move was to push the world. But the sliver's claw still twitched, red wounds appeared in Thed's chest, and ribbons of blood hung in the air."
—Adom Capashen, Benalish hero
Mages often seek to emulate the powerful relics lost to time and apocalypse.

"Take care what you offer the ignus. Food, perhaps. Coins. But nothing flammable!"
—Stovic, village eccentric

"A gargoyle's meat can be carved with an ordinary cleaver, but for its petrous hide . . ."
—Asmoranomardicadaistinaculdacar, *The Underworld Cookbook*
Tidal forces of the blood moon wrench and buckle the land, drawing monoliths of stone and soil toward the flaming orb.

"It's a testament to the forests' devastation that giant spiders now make their homes amid Dominaria's barren spires."
—Aznaph, greenseeker

"No ready! No aim! Just fire!"
—Scarback Plagg, orcish captain
Born of fire, destined for battle.

"Learn to burn!"
—Institute of Arcane Studies motto
Bred for battle in the Grand Coliseum, these wurms annihilated whole ecosystems when released into the wild.

"Echoes of the Mirari's power yet linger."
—Zyd, Kamahlite druid

"It's difficult to heal a rift after it begins wandering about on its own."
—Teferi

"It's rarely worth questioning where the mana comes from. Just be grateful."
—Jaya Ballard, task mage
In a shaman's grimy hands, a concoction of dried Skirk Ridge herbs can become the face of panic.
Dweldian magi don't enter the Realm of Thrones when they die. Instead their souls are drawn to great works of magic.
Arc mages aren't known for their patience.
The shaman of the tribe is responsible for keeping track of all its treasures, including angry pets and cursed lamps of fiery doom.

"That which would be a fatal mutation in any other species is merely a source of new powers. I am intrigued, yet too fearful to examine it more closely."
—Rukarumel, field journal
They seek out living trees to glean age-old secrets from sap and wood.
"At harvest are seeds of next year sown."

"When a sliver of this breed enters the hive, the others claw each other in frenzied fits, thereby ensuring their rapid growth."
—Rukarumel, field journal

"To those who can hear it, Gaea's battle song brings power as swift as sunlight and as enduring as the deep roots of the forest."
—Gamelen, Citanul elder

"The land is weary. Even Skyshroud is depleted. We must find another source of mana—one that is growing despite our withering world."
—Freyalise
"A rumor passes among the snakes, whispered by the rushes, inspiring the seekers: the goddess Freyalise is alive in Skyshroud."

"Life's greatest lessons don't come from focus or concentration. They come from breathing and simply noticing."
—Seton, centaur druid
His roots reach deep, nurtured not by soil and rain, but by millennia of experience.

"An ancient, powerful force has overtaken the valley. I sympathize for its former inhabitants, but I rejoice for the land itself."
—Olanti, Muraganda druid
Crovax sensed that Mirri wasn't ready for the curse taking hold of her. Weeping in his heart, he fled.

"Give up these unnatural weapons, these scrolls. Heart and mind and fist are enough."
—Zyd, Kamahlite druid

"It was a sight of pain and awe—a twisted forest, migrating across the salt plain in search of richer soil."
—Edahlis, greenseeker
"One day the vines of this forest will be as much a part of you as your own fingers."
Sometimes even humble forest creatures were gifted with mighty emanations from the past.

"The colossal thing rumbled over the ridge, tree husks crumbling before it. The ones we were already fighting howled as it came, their muscles suddenly surging, and we knew it was time to flee."
—Llanach, Skyshroud ranger
Some mages forsake their scrolls and libraries to learn at the feet of ancient trees and sacred stones.
The elder who carries the ancestral mantle of Jacques le Vert is tasked with his ancient mission: to protect the creatures of Pendelhaven.
When it snared a passing cockatrice, its own soul darkly doubled.
It died with the forest, yet both linger on in twisted form.
Their calls unheeded by the withered forests, nature shamans channeled the life force of their brethren.

"This sliver comes into the world a perfect predator. It's ready to hunt and devour its first meal within seconds of hatching."
—Rukarumel, field journal

"I am the simplifier, the root that drags all artifice to earth."
—Seal inscription
Each new generation of slivers evolves to assimilate the strengths of the prey upon which their progenitors fed.

"The hermit dies. The outcast dies. The lone wolf dies. Only those who stick together survive this world."
—Uros, Pendelhaven elder
What doesn't grow, dies. And what dies grows the tarmogoyf.
"The sight of my thallids still thriving is a bittersweet welcome to this cold waste."
Their arrows are tipped with basilisk eyes and fletched with cockatrice feathers.
Ground into the footprints of the ravaging herd were clumps of salt from Benalia, moss from Llanowar, dust from Hurloon, and ash from as far as Urborg.
"I'll guard this fruit and its seedling until the land is healed. My life now belongs to Dominaria."
The parched earth still shielded those few souls with the heart to call it home.

"At first we thought we were in some haunted wood. Then the branches twisted and scuttled toward us."
—Merrik Aidar, Benalish patrol

"It triggers the hive's period of aetheric fertility—a time when even feeding is a lower priority than reproduction."
—Rukarumel, field journal

"They are here, and they are hungry. And what they do not eat, they burn. Yavimaya is lost. We must leave now for Skyshroud."
—Edahlis, greenseeker
She wished for gold, but not for the strength to carry it.

"Since the last sliver arrived, even our mightiest relics splinter into shards as soon as we bring them against the hive."
—Llanach, Skyshroud ranger

"Rats and jackals feast in his swath, but even they will not walk with him."
—Mangara
Though Volrath is long dead, the slivers have become everything he wanted them to be: mindless instruments of destruction and despair.
"Run home, cur. I've already taken your master's head. Don't make me thrash you with it."
In the blink of an eye, she strode from deep snow to dusty waste. From the crease of light behind her, a voice rang hollow: "Saffi, wait for me . . . ."
Hidden within the clicking, chittering swarm is a unique mind, still young, but growing more aware as time passes.

"No rest. No mercy. No matter what."
—Memorial inscription

"This item is not from ... now. It reflects a sky no longer ours and gleams with hope that does not exist."
—Tavalus, acolyte of Korlis
The musical sound of its turning triggers the tumblers of revelation.
Rath's evincars used hivestones to control the slivers, but the overlay put their power into unwitting hands. Now the stones make not masters, but slaves.
A last wisp of paradise in a fallen world.
It bends not light but mana, aligning its chaotic currents into the sharp angles necessary for the mystic's purposes.
After centuries of labor, its creations outnumber those they were to mimic.

"Touch no tree, break no branch, and speak only the question you wish answered."
—Von Yomm, elder druid, to her initiates
Dust-spiked winds eroded the stones, but the ground where they had stood still holds power.

"They're still here?! The cockroach may have finally met its match."
—Teferi
Where scavengers nest in hollowed-out rib cages and chittering crawlers peer from empty eye sockets, few dare to trespass.
Take two steps north into the unsettled future, south into the unquiet past, east into the present day, or west into the great unknown.

"Yawgmoth's corpse is a wound in the universe. His foul blood seeps out, infecting the land with his final curse."
—Lord Windgrace

"Though their ideals are leagues apart, Urza's and Mishra's creations have a surprising harmony with one another."
—Tocasia, journal entry
It is everywhere you've ever been.

"When one of us prospers, the pride prospers."
—Jazal Goldmane
Some protection requires a bit of finesse.
Metal is scarce, smiths are pricey, and plate mail is heavy.
Its wings disturb more than air.
In life, they were a motley crew: farmers, lords, cutpurses, priests. In death, they are united in singular, benevolent purpose.
Unaware of Lorwyn's diversity, it sees only itself, reflected a thousand times over.
When Asha left Bant, she ensured that the world would have protection and order in her absence.

"Take a quiet moment to reflect on your sins."
—Cleph, Order of Redeemed Souls
"As this conflict grows, it gets harder to prevent the city from breaking down. How much longer can we keep this machinery balanced?"
It did not escape the ambassador's notice that the sound of war drums could also marshal the city to attention.
"If you've been at this as long as I have, nothing can surprise you. That's the hope, at least."
"The echo of silence is music to my ears."
"You are beneath contempt. Your lineage will be forgotten."
His mind whirled with grand plans, never thinking of what might happen if he were to succeed.
"Let the land dwellers know the coast is no longer the border between our realms. A new age of empire has begun."
The results of Rashmi's experimentation forced her to consider the possibility that multitudinous realities existed beyond her own.
"Well, at least all of that arm-waving and arcane babbling you did was impressive."

"Your deed cannot be undone. You, however, can be."
—Agosto, Azorius imperator
"The seas are vast, but the skies are even more so. Why be content with one kingdom when I can rule them both?"
Countless delights drift on the surface while dark schemes run below.

"You serve Phyrexia. Your pieces would better serve Phyrexia elsewhere."
—Azax-Azog, the Demon Thane
If everything in the Gurmag Swamp hungers for human flesh, what bait could be more effective?

"He is judge, jury, and executioner because he killed them all."
—Bishop Cawle of Elgaud
Where treachery and oblivion converge.
Her triumph came not from escaping her death, but in claiming her independence.
The dead know lessons the living haven't learned.

"Blood is constant. Every drop I drink, someone must bleed."
—Vradeen, vampire nocturnus
"Any dream is a robust harvest. Still, I prefer the timeworn dreams, heavy with import, that haunt the obsessive mind."
When the blood hunt lost its thrill, she looked for less tangible means of domination.
"Eldrazi? Ha! Try walking through Zulaport at night with your pockets full. Now *that's* dangerous."
"Greet death with sword in hand."
There was no reason to pray. This was already an act of the gods.
The storm rages and the earth breaks.
Chandra's gift set her apart and others aflame.
"She will come back to me."
Some kami attacks during the war were rife with trickery, subterfuge, and subtlety, draining hope and pride from the mortal world. Other attacks were a lot more straightforward.
When the molten rains fall, entire landscapes melt and flow away in rivulets of fire.
The calligraphy of combat is written with strokes of sudden blood.
Beauty is in the eye of the exploder.
Immolation is the sincerest form of flattery.
"The tiniest mouse speaks louder to me than all the festival crowds on Tin Street."

"Kill the weak so they can't drag the strong down to their level. This is true compassion."
—Benzir, archdruid of Temple Might

"Life grows everywhere. My kin merely find those places where it grows strongest."
—Nissa Revane
She remembers every word spoken, from the hero's oath to the baby's cry.
The essence of nature is change.
"How truly vast this city must be, that I have traveled so far and seen so much, yet never once found the place where the buildings fail."

"The timeless, tireless jaws of nature shall one day devour us all."
—Sildark, artificer of Omu
When nature calls, *run*.
"What was once formed by masons, shaped by smiths, or given life by mages, I will return to the embrace of the earth."

"As long as there is a single shred of life, there is hope."
—Nissa Revane

"Always carry two spears."
—Mokgar, Kalonian hunter

"When the kumo attacked the monks' sacred shrine, a mournful toll for help echoed through the forest. Thus began the Battle of Silk, which would last six years."
—*Great Battles of Kamigawa*
The Izzet quickly suspended their policy of lifetime guarantees.
Forked tails rustled. Talons clicked. A lone sliver streaked overhead like jagged lightning, and the hive thundered.
"I see you've learned nothing, Chandra. You'd still put a match to something rather than understand it."
The eyes let flow with tears, then blood, then the very soul—the whole wrung inside out, dripping down into the blackened puddle of the past.
An elder in one pride, of the Sigiled caste in another.
Rakshasa trade in secrets, amassing wealth from their careful revelation.
As Jhoira restored the *Weatherlight*, a mushroom growing in its hold unexpectedly became her first crew member.
Held aloft by metabolized magic, trygons are ravenous for sources of mystic fuel.
The vedalken know it is not of this world, so they know that this world is not the only one.

"You've begun to understand the hedrons' true purpose," said Ugin. "The Eldrazi can be imprisoned."
"And how did that work out last time?" asked Jace.
The embodiment of yearning, forever drifting the deserts to find what had once made it whole.
Once a century, the levelers rip through every corner of Mirrodin, obeying the commands of an unseen master.

"Locks want to be opened, and treasure wants to be free."
—Nayrex Slipfinger, master thief
All who listen hear their own song, a unique melody played just for them.
Taj-Nar, throne of Raksha Golden Cub, destined leader of the leonin prides.
"There is always opportunity to improve your useless minions, Shredder . . . just as you 'improved' me."
"Yo, Rock! These dudes got hard candy shells!"
"Do not regret being defeated by me; my design made my victory inevitable."
"A war is coming that will spread from the streets of this city and engulf the entire world."
"Weak words. Weak actions! I have forever known what you fail to understand: Strength . . . Always . . . Prevails!"
"Family? We ain't no family, ya. Monsters got no kin."
"I am the chaos in the cracks, the vermin in the shadows. Everything fears me . . . everything except the rats."
"Let's crack 'em open and see what kinda goodies are inside!"
"You make it all so easy. Hmm, shall I freeze you in time forever? Devolve you back into four little sea dinosaurs and a monkey? Ooh! Or perhaps primal sludge."
"There is undoubtedly a fascinating story in how my old nemesis came to teach ninjitsu to four mutant turtles . . . perhaps I will let one of you live long enough to tell it!"
"You have a true warrior's spirit, you four, just like me. Except for the part where you hold back!"
"I suppose this is where I should be feeling pity . . ."
"Definitely feels good to be on the winning side of a beatdown."
"Threat detected. Eliminate."
"The future belongs to those who can take it."
"I don't know how you found your way into my war . . . but I promise you will rue the day you chose to oppose me."
"Think you can take on the apex predator o' dese parts? I dun think so, ya."
"The road we all trod—well, that you all trod—has one and only one destination."
"We wanna go bigger! We want the next fight to be freak against freak."

"You shall be forever stuck in the confines of time."
—Savanti Romero
"Yes, come forward! Attack me if you will. When it is over, you will call me Master!"
"If you're gonna be free, you need to lose some dead weight . . ."
"Ninjas. Vanish!"

"We will destroy EVERYTHING!"
—Bebop & Rocksteady

"No underling will ever consider me to be only as strong as my armor. And no one will stand in my way."
—Krang
A ninja's deadliest strike can come from anywhere, even from above.
The Shredder demands much of the Foot ninjas, and few live up to his expectations. However, their masks do more than hide their identity; they hide a brutal turnover rate.
Ultimately, all the Foot require of their enemies is fear. When stealth fails, strength will suffice.
"Their chanting grows louder as the tide rises." —Tamiyo's journal

n: Nissa, Who Shakes the World Emblem
